title: Former Zhao
capsule: Zhao was one of the seven major states of the Warring States period, created in 403 BCE when the Zhou king formally recognised the tripartite division of Jin alongside Han and Wei. King Wuling (r. 325–299 BCE) transformed the state militarily by adopting nomadic cavalry tactics — the 'Barbarian Dress' reforms — which allowed Zhao to defeat Zhongshan and rival Qin temporarily. The decisive blow fell at the Battle of Changping in 260 BCE, where Qin's army annihilated Zhao's forces under the replaced general Zhao Kuo, killing an estimated 400,000 captives; Zhao never recovered its offensive capability. Qin's general Wang Jian conquered the Zhao capital Handan in 228 BCE after king Youmiao had been induced to execute the competent Li Mu; a remnant government at Dai held out until 222 BCE.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Zhao's territorial extent is attested in the Shiji and Zhan Guo Ce and corroborated by archaeological finds; borders with Wei, Yan, and Qin were contested and shifted frequently, making precise mapping of any given year uncertain.
